extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2024 reviewers (assigned reviewers and program committee members)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating machine learning research submissions to ICLR 2024 using the conference's reviewer guidance: answer the core evaluation questions, follow required review structure, comply with ethical requirements, and participate in discussion phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and substantive evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: "Reviews must ensure that evaluations are 'timely and substantive'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reviews on schedule and with meaningful, detailed feedback. The role is described as "central to the program creation process," so lateness or perfunctory reviews undermine the conference. Timeliness includes participating in discussion phases and updating assessments if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to Code of Ethics and Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must adhere to the Code of Ethics and Code of Conduct while performing reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professional, respectful behavior in reviews and discussion; avoid inappropriate comments, conflicts of interest, or breaches of confidentiality. Flag suspected ethical issues through the required channels (see Code of Ethics report requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem statement clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: What specific problem does the paper tackle?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the submission clearly identifies the target problem, its scope, and why it matters. Consider originality and relevance of the problem formulation and whether authors situate the problem relative to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach motivation and positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the approach well-motivated and properly positioned in literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the method is justified (theoretical/empirical rationale) and whether the paper accurately and fairly situates itself with respect to related work. Note missing citations only when they materially affect evaluation (see 'recent work' guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Results support claims with correctness and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Do results support the claims with correctness and scientific rigor?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check correctness of proofs/derivations, rigor of experiments, appropriateness of baselines, statistical validity, and whether conclusions follow from presented evidence. Flag technical errors or unsupported claims and request clarifications when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution: new, relevant, impactful knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the work contribute "new, relevant, impactful knowledge" to the community?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the novelty and potential impact of the paper: incremental vs. substantive advances, generality/applicability, and relevance to the ICLR community. Acceptance does not require top-tier state-of-the-art performance if novelty and impact are convincing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required review structure and elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must include: summary of paper's contributions (positive, constructive tone); comprehensive lists of strengths and weaknesses; clear initial recommendation with key justifications; supporting arguments for the recommendation; clarifying questions for authors; constructive feedback for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise, neutral summary of contributions first. List strengths and weaknesses explicitly and substantively. Give an explicit recommendation (e.g., accept/weak accept/weak reject/reject) and the main reasons for it. Include concrete suggestions for improvement and specific questions authors should answer in rebuttal. Maintain constructive, professional tone throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-of-the-art not required
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prematurely reject work solely because it does not beat existing top results. Focus on whether the paper "convincingly demonstrates new, relevant, impactful knowledge." Consider theoretical contributions, new problem formulations, analyses, or insights that advance understanding even without SOTA metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials are optional reading
rubrics_metrics.description: "Supplementary materials may clarify questions but aren't mandatory reading."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary evaluation should be based on the main paper. Use supplementary material to resolve important technical questions when necessary, but a reviewer is not expected to treat every supplementary detail as required reading; flag critical missing information in the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling recent work citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers published within four months of submission deadline need not be cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be pragmatic about very recent concurrent work; absence of citations to work within the four-month window should not be held against authors. Focus on whether the paper acknowledges and positions itself relative to relevant prior work available at time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Ethics report and flagging violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must complete a Code of Ethics report flagging potential violations during submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suspect ethical issues (e.g., data misuse, authorship concerns, plagiarism), report them through the prescribed Code of Ethics reporting mechanism. Provide evidence or clear rationale for the flag to assist program chairs in investigating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in discussions and openness to change
rubrics_metrics.description: During the asynchronous discussion phase reviewers should remain "open to changing" recommendations based on author responses and peer feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage actively in the discussion phase, answer clarifying questions, consider author rebuttals and peers' perspectives, and update your assessment if new information justifies it. Treat borderline cases flexibly and use discussion to resolve disagreements.
